strings.app.title: How to read this report
strings.app.intro: This page explains the colours and the terms used in this report. It describes what the numbers mean; it does not tell anyone what to do.
strings.app.key.title: Colour key
strings.app.key.lead: A level is judged on the lower of the two newest clear satellite days, so one odd day cannot move it.
strings.app.key.GREEN.when: Chlorophyll is below the usual high for this time of year and is not climbing.
strings.app.key.YELLOW.when: Chlorophyll is at or above the usual high for this time of year (the top 1 in 10 of past values), or it is above normal and has been rising for 3 days.
strings.app.key.ORANGE.when: Chlorophyll is at or above the very high mark for this time of year (the top 3 in 100), or a yellow plant has an upstream monitoring point at least 1.5 times its own usual high (an upstream signal).
strings.app.key.RED.when: Chlorophyll is at least 3 times the normal for this time of year and at or above the usual high, or the plant was orange or red yesterday and is orange again today (two days running).
strings.app.key.RED.means: Far outside the normal range, or unusual again after an unusual day.
strings.app.key.GREY.when: There was no clear satellite view in the last 3 days, less than a quarter of the area was visible, or there is not enough past data for this time of year.
strings.app.key.GREY.means: No level can be given. Grey is never an all-clear.
strings.app.gl.title: Terms
strings.app.gl.chl.d: A green pigment in algae. Satellites measure it as a sign of how much algae there is in the surface water.
strings.app.gl.unit.d: Milligrams of chlorophyll-a in one cubic metre of seawater. The higher the number, the more algae.
strings.app.gl.normal.t: Normal for this time of year
strings.app.gl.normal.d: The comparison is with the same time of year since 2020, in the same area and from the same satellite. Normal: not in the top quarter of past values. Above normal: the top quarter. High: the top 1 in 10. Very high: the top 3 in 100. Far above normal: at least 3 times the usual middle. The technical details give the exact marks (the 50th, 75th, 90th and 97th percentiles).
strings.app.gl.sats.d: The sharp satellite sees the sea in 4 km squares and gives the most detailed view, but cloud often blocks it. The smoothed satellite uses 9 km squares and fills the gaps from neighbouring days and places, so it almost always has a value but shows fewer small patches. The report uses the sharp one when it has a recent clear view and the smoothed one otherwise. Because they see the sea differently, a level can change on the day the report switches from one to the other even though the water did not change; the report says so when that happens.
strings.app.gl.sure.d: Good: a clear view of more than half of the area, at most 2 days old, from the sharp satellite. Limited: only part of the area was clear, the view is 3 days old, or only the smoothed satellite was available. Low: no level could be given.
strings.app.gl.upstream.d: Places along the coast (Port Said, El-Arish and Rafah for the Mediterranean plants; the Strait of Tiran and mid-gulf for Eilat) where algae can show up before they reach the intake. A plant's level can be raised when such a point is far above its own usual high.
strings.app.gl.shared.d: Two plants whose areas fall on exactly the same satellite squares get exactly the same readings, so they are not two independent confirmations.
strings.app.gl.delay.d: Satellite data arrive about 2 days after the pass, so the newest view is usually from 2 days ago, not from today.
strings.app.gl.sst.d: Shown in the technical details only; it never changes a level. Warm water (26 °C or more and at least 1 °C above normal) favours very small algae called picocyanobacteria.
strings.app.lim.title: Limits
strings.app.lim.1: The satellite sees only the top few metres of the sea.
strings.app.lim.2: Cloud, dust and sun glare hide the sea or distort the reading.
strings.app.lim.3: Squares near the shore are less reliable.
strings.app.lim.4: A satellite square is bigger than an intake, so a patch next to the intake can be missed or averaged away.
strings.app.lim.5: "Normal" rests on only about six years of history.
strings.app.lim.6: This is an early warning, not a measurement at the intake.
strings.app.lim.7: The plant's own online analysers remain the real-time alarm.
strings.app.src.title: Where the numbers come from
strings.app.src.n20: Sharp satellite chlorophyll-a (NOAA, the VIIRS sensor on the NOAA-20 satellite, 4 km)
strings.app.src.dineof: Smoothed satellite chlorophyll-a (NOAA, gaps filled with the DINEOF method, 9 km)
strings.app.src.sst: Sea surface temperature (NOAA Coral Reef Watch, CoralTemp)
strings.app.src.coast: Coastline on the map (Natural Earth, public domain)
strings.app.src.rules: The exact rules, marks and the reasons for them are in docs/scoring.md and docs/reading-the-report.md in the project.
